beats.text: Photo 51 had two names behind it.
beats.note: KCL and UKRI say it was taken by Rosalind Franklin with her PhD student Raymond Gosling at King's College London in May 1952.

beats.context: King's College London says the DNA was exposed to X rays for a total of 62 hours to take Photograph 51.

beats.note: KCL says Wilkins showed it to him, having a copy because he was soon to take over the work. KCL says Franklin was unaware.

beats.text: Wilkins had it legitimately, says UKRI.
beats.note: UKRI says it was part of her papers as she was leaving for Birkbeck, and notes some people think he should not have shared it without her knowledge or permission.

beats.name: Nature, 25 April
beats.role: KCL says Photograph 51 was published in a paper by Franklin and Gosling, in the same issue as Watson and Crick's paper.

beats.text: The 1962 Nobel Prize went to three men.
beats.note: Wilkins, Watson and Crick shared it. Franklin died in 1958, and History notes the Nobel Foundation does not award prizes posthumously.

beats.text: The evidence was public in 1953. The prize came nine years later.
